ops.title: rm guard: macOS trash rewrite — glob >10 stays blocked BY DESIGN
ops.body:
General pack 0.26.0 / repo 9.29.0 (commit ae212caf, 2026-07-18): on macOS with a resolvable `trash` binary, the rm guard rewrites recoverably-risky deletes to `<trash path> <targets>` instead of denying — but ONLY for literal outside-repo targets and globs whose ≤`GLOB_LIMIT` matches were each individually verified.

**Globs matching >10 files and too-broad globs deny on every platform — this is a deliberate post-review narrowing, not a regression.** Adversarial verification confirmed by execution that rewriting them trashes a repo root hiding beyond the `limit+1` collection prefix (`rm -rf *` in a directory with >11 entries, repo at position 12+), violating the user-decided repo-root-always-blocks invariant. Do not "restore" the oversized-glob rewrite without solving exhaustive match verification.

Emission soundness rests on provenance gates in `emit_target` / `block_risky_rm` (captain_hook/packs/general/deletions.py): `plain_words` (no quote chars in `Command.raw`) gates verbatim emission of glob/tilde tokens; brace tokens and non-provenanced backslash tokens forfeit the rewrite; a `\`-newline continuation anywhere in the occurrence forfeits it (cc-transcript splits `foo\⏎bar` into two args where the shell joins to `foobar`); the trash path is shlex-quoted. All confirmed against cc_transcript's parser by execution.

Tag v9.29.0 NOT cut — commit sits on local branch `rm-trash-rewrite` (detached-HEAD anchor) because the working copy carries another session's in-flight export-registry refactor; push/tag after that settles.
